spec.title: JBMC read through --json-ui agrees with the text reading on every recorded JBMC example (step 4b of the sound-verdicts brief)
spec.description: Step 4b of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md: jvmcontract now reads JBMC through --json-ui (lib/src/jbmc.rs parse_json: the property results, the failed property's trace with input values read from their bits, and the overall cProverStatus) instead of its console text, and each run records how it ended (search.runs[].ending: verified, counterexample, unwinding-failure, other-failure, timeout, memory-exhausted, killed, solver-failure, unsupported-input, unavailable, unreadable). The brief keeps the text parser only until a differential test over every recorded JBMC example shows the two agree. This job is that test: it copies examples/ to a scratch directory and runs build.py there on the 41 recorded B9/B11 examples proved by JBMC on the javac apps (Quorum, Crosscut, Mica), with JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_READ=both, which runs every JBMC invocation twice, with --json-ui and without, decides by the JSON, and appends what each reading made of the run (verdict, ending, property count, the counterexample's inputs in one canonical form) to differential.jsonl. Nothing in the repository's examples changes. The inline integration test the_json_and_the_text_reading_of_jbmc_agree already checks four cases on the real JBMC 6.11.0 (six runs: a proof, counterexamples over an int[] and a long, an unwinding failure).
spec.expected: exits 0, printing 'ok: the JSON and the text reading agree on every run of every recorded JBMC example, and every verdict is as expected', after a line counting the runs read both ways (some 100 or more) with 0 disagreeing. A DISAGREE line names a log and what differs (verdict, ending, counterexample or property count): that is a bug in one of the readers, most likely the JSON one, to fix before the text reader is removed. A build.py exit of 1 means a recorded verdict moved under the JSON reading; build.txt names the example.

resources.notes: the 41 examples' recorded JBMC proof lines add up to about 150 s; every run is made twice here, with the interval stages, and build.py compiles and tests the app for each example (some 20-30 s each); JBMC is capped at 3 GiB

steps.name: 41 recorded JBMC examples, read both ways
steps.run:
set -eo pipefail
W=lib/target/jobs/4b-differential; rm -rf "$W"; mkdir -p "$W/repo"
# build.py writes results into the examples folder it runs from: a copy, so nothing recorded changes.
cp -r examples "$W/repo/"
(cd lib && cargo build --release -q)
export JVMCONTRACT="$PWD/lib/target/release/jvmcontract" JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_READ=both JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_DIFFERENTIAL="$PWD/$W/differential.jsonl"
IDS=$(python3 examples/tools/build.py --plan | python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(" ".join(p["example"] for p in json.load(sys.stdin) if p["approach"] in ("B9", "B11") and p.get("engine") == "jbmc" and p.get("app") in ("quorum", "crosscut", "mica") and p["executable"]))')
echo "examples: $IDS"
status=0; python3 "$W/repo/examples/tools/build.py" $IDS > "$W/build.txt" 2>&1 || status=$?
tail -5 "$W/build.txt"
python3 - "$W/differential.jsonl" "$status" <<'PY'
import json, sys
lines = [json.loads(l) for l in open(sys.argv[1])]
bad = [d for d in lines if not d["agree"]]
endings = {}
for d in lines:
    endings[d["json"]["ending"]] = endings.get(d["json"]["ending"], 0) + 1
print(f"{len(lines)} JBMC runs read both ways, {len(bad)} disagreeing; endings from the JSON: {endings}")
for d in bad:
    print("DISAGREE", d["log"], d["stage"], d["differences"])
assert lines, "no JBMC run was read both ways"
assert not bad, "the readings disagree"
assert sys.argv[2] == "0", f"build.py exited {sys.argv[2]}: a verdict differs from its expected one (see build.txt)"
print("ok: the JSON and the text reading agree on every run of every recorded JBMC example, and every verdict is as expected")
PY
